# Handover: plan to implement

## Summary

The slide animation respects reduced motion. Keyboard focus moves through the rail in reading order and returns to it after a page loads. The audit is run per page and the results are listed below. Icon-only controls have accessible names from the i18n catalog. The settings route and its five sub-pages use the shared NavRail. This handover closes the plan stage and opens implement.

## What changed

- `web/settings/pages/Security.vue`: moved into the new layout; the password dialog returns focus to its opener.
- `web/components/NavRail.vue`: shared rail component; roving focus, arrow keys and Home and End.
- `web/settings/pages/Notifications.vue`: moved into the new layout; toggles keep their labels.
- `tests/a11y/settings.audit.ts`: axe audit per page; violations written to a report file.
- `web/router/settings.ts`: routes for the five sub-pages under one parent with the rail as layout.
- `web/styles/motion.css`: slide animation of the rail respects prefers-reduced-motion.
- `web/settings/pages/Billing.vue`: moved into the new layout; data calls untouched as the brief asks.
- `web/settings/pages/Integrations.vue`: moved into the new layout; the list loads in a lazy chunk.
- `web/i18n/en/a11y.json`: new accessible names for the icon-only controls, keys only, no literals in templates.
- `tests/e2e/settings-keyboard.spec.ts`: keyboard-only pass through all five sub-pages.
- `tests/component/NavRail.spec.ts`: keyboard cases for the rail: arrows, wrap, Home, End, focus return.
- `web/settings/SettingsLayout.vue`: uses NavRail in place of the old tab bar; the content slot is unchanged.
- `docs/settings-nav.md`: how the rail works, its focus rules and the audit command.
- `web/settings/pages/Profile.vue`: moved into the new layout, no content change.

## Decisions and why

1. Use roving tabindex in the rail. Why: one tab stop keeps the reading order short for keyboard users.
2. Return focus to the rail after a sub-page loads. Why: users lost their place when the page content replaced the focused element.
3. Disable the slide animation under reduced motion. Why: the setting is a requirement from the accessibility review.
4. Run the audit per page, not per route group. Why: violations differ by page and a group result hides them.
5. Keep page contents as they are. Why: the brief limits the task to navigation and the audit.
6. Add i18n keys for every icon-only control. Why: literals would bypass translation and the screen-reader text would stay English.
7. Leave billing data calls alone. Why: another task changes that API at the same time.

## Open risks

- **Blocking risk**: The audit has not been run on the integrations page yet.
- The component tests mock the router; a real navigation is covered only by the end-to-end pass.
- The rail has no visible focus ring in forced-colors mode; the shared theme does not define one.
- The security page dialog returns focus correctly, but only when opened by keyboard.
- The axe audit reports one moderate colour-contrast violation on the notifications page that comes from the shared theme.
- The new i18n keys exist in English only; translators have not seen them.

## How verified

- Tabbed through each page in reading order and compared with the design notes.
- Checked the rail with the OS reduced-motion setting on and off; the slide is skipped when on.
- Keyboard-only end-to-end pass through all five pages completes without a mouse.
- Component tests for the rail pass: 18 cases, including wrap-around and focus return.
- Axe audit run on each page; results listed in the audit section below.
- Ran the layout in the narrow viewport; the rail collapses to the menu button.

## Not touched

Nothing outside the files above changed. Generated files, vendored code and the other tasks' folders were left alone on purpose; if a diff shows them, the cause is a tool, not this stage.

## Next step guidance

- Run the audit on each page yourself; the report file is regenerated by the command.
- Review focus order first; it is the main acceptance point of the brief.
- Check the rail in the narrow viewport; the menu button has its own focus rules.
- Do not add content changes to the pages; send them back to the owner.
